title: The Unknowing Lab
description: 🌿 Description An experiential workshop blending nervous system science with meditation, somatic practice, and relational exercises. 🌿 About This Gathering Most of us have spent a lot of our lives collecting knowledge, figuring things out, and trying to stay in control. In the age of AI, information is more abundant than ever. What we need now may be the capacity to step out of cognitive loops, meet uncertainty, listen to our innate intelligence, and embody forms of wisdom beyond the analytical mind. The Unknowing Lab is an exploration of science, spirituality, and the art of not knowing. Across contemplative traditions, we find teachings that invite us to relax the conceptual mind and experience reality more directly. Neuroscience, psychology, and nervous system research are now giving us new ways to understand why these practices can be transformative—and why letting go of familiar identities, predictions, and patterns can also feel vulnerable. We’ll explore some of that science, but we won’t stop at analyzing it. We’ll become our own researchers, using meditation, somatic practice, play, and relational inquiry to discover what unknowing actually feels like in the body. This is a space to move from insight to embodiment: to let the nervous system rest, loosen habitual patterns, open to creativity and possibility, and meet life with a little less friction and a little more curiosity, trust, and participation. 🕝 Schedule We'll begin at 6:30, and doors will open 10 minutes beforehand. 🕰 Flow Arrival + Nervous System Grounding Guided somatic practices to help your nervous system balance, release physical & mental tension, and arrive in the present moment. Science + Spiritual Wisdom A grounded introduction to unknowing and the relationship between awareness, nervous system regulation, and loosening the conceptual self. Embodied Practices Gentle regulation, resourcing, meditation, and playful experiments that invite curiosity and new ways of perceiving. Relational Inquiry Partner practices where we experiment with staying present, connected, and open while investigating our relationship to unknowing. Integration + Closing Reflecting on what we discovered and how it might live beyond the workshop. 👥 Facilitator Pauline Romas is a somatic facilitator, community builder, and lifelong student of the divine mystery. She brings her background as an engineer and thousands of hours of meditation practice to her work with embodiment and the nervous system. Pauline creates spaces of unconditional acceptance where people can connect with their heart’s wisdom and inner guidance to explore new ways of living and relating, bringing their spiritual insights into everyday life. Learn more about Pauline and her work at PaulineRomas.love 💫 Who This Is For This gathering is for curious humans who spend a lot of time in their heads, feel drawn to the intersection of science and spirituality, or long to embody what they already know intellectually. No particular belief system or meditation experience is required—only a willingness to be curious, experiment, and explore. 🎒 What to Bring Suggested: comfortable clothes you can move in, water bottle, journal. 🏛 About The Commons The Commons is a community-based "Fourth Place" that catalyzes each member's path to authenticity, full self-expression, and aliveness - rooted in the belief that community is essential to that journey. Located in the heart of San Francisco, we are redefining what it means to gather, work, and connect. By day, we're a playful co-working space; by night, a vibrant community meeting house. 🚪 Arrival Info The Commons is located at 550 Laguna St, San Francisco (corner of Hayes & Laguna). Enter via the stairway under The Commons sign at the basement level.

title: The Commons Camping Retreat
description: 🌲 The Commons Camping Retreat September 24–27, 2026 · Shimmerback Ranch, near Willits, CA 🌿 About Event What happens when we take The Commons out of the city and into the woods? For four days, we’re heading north to Shimmerback Ranch—nearly 150 acres of forest, creek, trails, and gathering spaces about 2.5 hours from San Francisco—to experiment with a slower, more communal rhythm of life. Think of it as a temporary Commons village: waking up among the trees, cooking and eating together, swimming in the creek, making things with our hands, sharing skills and ideas, tending the land, and having the kind of long, wandering conversations that become possible when nobody has somewhere else to be in an hour. During the day, we’ll invite members to offer workshops, creative practices, facilitated conversations, crafts, music, and whatever else they’d like to share. Some time may also be devoted to hands-on stewardship projects around the property—an opportunity to learn practical skills while giving something back to the land hosting us. And when evening arrives? We’ll gather around food and fire, make music, and—far from our usual sound-sensitive neighbors—perhaps finally answer the important civic question: what does a Commons rave look like in the middle of the woods? ✨🌲🔊 This retreat is an experiment in community beyond the walls of 540 and 550: a chance to rest, play, collaborate, and discover what becomes possible when we have a little more time and space with one another. 🕰 Flow / Schedule This will be a Thursday–Sunday retreat, with plenty of spacious, unscheduled time built in. Thursday, September 24 Arrival, camp setup, orientation, shared dinner, and settling into the land. Friday & Saturday 🌲 Slow mornings and shared meals 🛠 Member-led workshops and skill-sharing 🎨 Art, crafting, building, and creative projects 🌿 Optional land stewardship projects 💧 Creek swimming and time to explore or simply rest 🍲 Communal cooking and meals 🎶 Music, jams, dancing, and nighttime gatherings Sunday, September 27 A final morning together, shared cleanup and stewardship of the space, packing up, and heading home. A more detailed schedule—and opportunities to propose workshops—will be shared as the retreat takes shape. 👥 Facilitators The retreat is being organized by Cody Hasty and The Commons, with the weekend itself shaped collaboratively by the members who attend. Rather than bringing in a fixed program of teachers, we’re imagining something closer to a community unconference: Commons members sharing the skills, practices, questions, and creative pursuits they care about. Want to teach something, facilitate a conversation, DJ a set, lead a craft, cook for the group, organize a game, or contribute another offering? We’d love for you to help shape the weekend. 💫 Who This Is For This retreat is for Commons members who want to spend meaningful time together outside the rhythms of everyday city life. You do not need to be an experienced camper, outdoorsperson, workshop facilitator, or wilderness mystic. 🌿 Come if you’re excited to: deepen friendships and make new ones learn and share skills create things alongside other people spend a few days surrounded by nature contribute to communal meals and shared responsibilities dance, play, rest, swim, wander, talk, or simply exist around a campfire together The heart of the weekend is participation rather than performance. You can offer a workshop or just show up ready to lend a hand. 🎒 What to Bring (Optional) A detailed packing list will be shared with attendees before the retreat. For now, plan for several days of camping and outdoor life, including warm layers for evenings, sturdy shoes, personal toiletries, a flashlight or headlamp, and whatever you need to sleep comfortably. If you have camping equipment, musical instruments, games, art supplies, crafting tools, or something you’d enjoy sharing with the group, you’re welcome to bring them. Please do not store food or other bear attractants inside tents. We’ll coordinate safe food storage on-site. Don't own camping gear? Don't let that stop you from expressing interest—we'll see what we can share and coordinate as a community. 💛 Suggested Donation / Exchange Our goal is to make the retreat as financially accessible as possible. The maximum anticipated land cost is approximately $130 per person for the full Thursday–Sunday retreat ($32.50/day). Depending on attendance, Commons support, and opportunities to exchange volunteer stewardship projects for part of the cost, your actual price may be lower—or potentially free. We’ll confirm the final contribution once we have a reliable headcount. For those who would rather not sleep in a tent, a limited number of upgraded accommodations—including a bunkhouse, tiny houses, an RV, and glamping options—may be available for an additional cost. 🏛 About The Commons The Commons is a civic temple for wisdom, belonging, and beauty in San Francisco—a place to practice community rather than simply talk about it. We believe belonging grows through shared experience: learning together, making things together, caring for spaces together, celebrating together, and showing up for one another. This retreat takes that experiment beyond our walls. For a few days, instead of simply gathering at The Commons, we get to practice building a little commons of our own. 🚪 Arrival Info 📍 Shimmerback Ranch · near Willits, California 🚗 Approximately 2.5 hours north of San Francisco Exact directions, arrival instructions, transportation coordination, campsite information, lodging assignments, and a packing guide will be sent to confirmed attendees before the retreat. Because this is an offsite retreat rather than an event at our usual San Francisco home, please RSVP rather than simply showing up. We’ll also coordinate carpools and transportation as the group comes together. 🌲 Come for the woods. Bring something to share. Help us build the village for a weekend.

title: What Should Stay Human When Agents Join the Team?
description: Your team works with AI agents now, and nobody has agreed what the agents get to decide. So everyone draws their own line. One person lets the agent send the client email. Another rewrites everything it touches. Someone hides how much they use it. None of it gets said out loud, and slowly the team stops trusting the work, and each other. This workshop is where a team draws the line together: which calls stay human, which go to the agents, and which the agent drafts and a human decides. What you leave with is a one-page agreement your team wrote, and a monthly practice to keep it current as the work changes. WHO IT'S FOR: Founders and team leads bringing AI agents into a team, and anyone on a team that already works with them. Heads of HR / People & Culture who want a way to do this across teams. LEAVE WITH: A one-page team agreement: what stays human, what goes to the agents, what needs a human check. A 45-minute monthly version you can run with your own team.

title: Command Line Music - Auwen Workshop
description: This class is an intro to command line music with Auwen, a tool for writing and performing songs in real time using a command line interface. You'll get hands-on experience building tracks from scratch and playing them in a low stakes, collaborative setting. No prior coding or music experience needed. What to expect: installation takes about 5 minutes. Your first beat, maybe an hour. Playing a full set takes a 3-6 weeks of practice depending on experience level. A few students have gone on to perform live sets at SF events and festivals as part of Soniare Collective. With just a bit of dedication you could be next! We would love to have you join our growing family of music producers. After the class you'll be invited to our Discord where we do multiplayer jam sessions, so there's space to keep learning and playing with other people. Workshop Outline Software and sample installation Overview of Auwen User Interface and workflow Multiplayer learning session creating genres you suggest Solo time creating music on your own computer Wrap-up and share resources for further learning Educational Goals To inspire participants and offer an accessible entry point into performing live dance music, while building foundational skills in livecoding, composition, improvisation, and real-time musical decision-making. Instructor Nes Croft is a musician, artist, and computer engineer from Montana who has written and recorded thousands of songs since a young age starting with folk/rock as a teenager and expanding into experimental pop, IDM, techno, and trance. Nes gained an interest in electronics at age 19 after working at the DIY synth company Synthrotek in Portland, OR. Going on to earn a bachelor's degree in computer engineering at Montana State University. While in college Nes co-founded and developed Vaytricks Beat Machine, a mobile drum machine app that received over 100,000 downloads. 5 years later Nes left Vaytricks to pursue a live performance focused approach to music production and Auwen was born. Auwen is a digital audio workstation featuring a hybrid producer/DJ workflow that allows musicians to perform dance music live using a command line interface. Given the nature of the software, Nes naturally gravitated toward live music events testing Auwen at various electronic music festivals in Montana. Later, Nes joined the livecoding scene in San Francisco and started hosting workshops & live music events at TIAT art gallery and Gray Area in San Francisco in 2025-2026. Preparation Bring a laptop/headphones and install the software auwen.app to save time in class. Also bring water and maybe a light snack to keep your energy up because we'll be covering a lot of information! Some drinks may be provided as well. When you arrive come through the front of TIAT then all the way back and down the stairs on the left. The event is in the TIAT basement.

description: Being Here is a weekly gathering guided by Dharma Teacher Milo Burn, who has led multiple three-month silent retreats and teaches from a background grounded in Zen and Theravada practice. So much of our lives are oriented toward becoming. Being Here offers a regular space to pause that momentum and explore what becomes possible when we give our attention to simply being here. Through meditation, heart teachings, and conversation, we practice bringing this quality of being into the rest of our lives. The emphasis is on direct experience rather than technique. Think: less following a recipe and more hanging out in your grandma’s kitchen! Come to practice, listen, ask questions, or spend time in a space devoted to being. title: The Commons Public Hours ☕
description: 🎉 Public Hours at the Commons 🎉 Every Sunday, the Commons opens to the public — no membership required. Come co-work, connect, create, or just explore the space at your own pace. ✨ 🕘 When: Every Sunday, 9 AM – 10 PM 📍 Where: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco (corner of Hayes & Laguna, basement level) RSVP and we'll email you your entry code ahead of time — so you can let yourself straight in when you arrive. ────────────────────────────── 🧭 A self-guided day Public Hours are self-guided — come in, settle in, and make the space your own. Weekends are usually unstaffed, so there's no check-in desk or guided tour. Our members are glad to answer questions about the space; for anything else — including guided tours, which we don't offer as drop-ins — email hello@thesfcommons.com ahead of time. ────────────────────────────── 🔭 Getting in Your entry code comes by email. Once you RSVP, we'll send you a personal QR code — that's your key for the day. Keep it handy on your phone (and check spam if you don't see it). Find us. title: From Pain to Resource: Embodied Awareness, Posture & Movement
description: Join me for a gentle exploration of the body, guided by functional anatomy and embodied awareness. I’ll share some of my own journey from experiencing my body as pain to discovering it as a reliable resource for grounding, rest, and guidance. My work is rooted in the Alexander Technique and has evolved through ten years of self-practice and teaching, meditation, and emotional healing. Over the past two years, brain retraining for mold sensitivity and energy practices have further broadened my understanding and informed my approach. Through experiential practices, we’ll explore how subtle holding patterns we may not notice can shape our posture and contribute to pain, and what can happen when we make contact with what is already there rather than trying to change it. Depending on time and interest, I may demonstrate hands-on guidance with a volunteer. description: Hey, I'm Chelsea. I was diagnosed with depression and anxiety at 28 years old. I always struggled with meaningful connection and often shut down in social situations. What I learned through finding support is that I don't have to feel this way and I can't do it alone. In this interactive gathering, we'll have the space to explore what social anxiety feels like and how we can build tools to overcome it together. While healing is a continuous journey and I am far from done, I have spent the last 10 years building spaces and collecting the tools that I wish I had when I was younger. Through that process, I obtained my Masters in Mental Health Counseling and have used that training to grow the You Aren't Alone Project, a nonprofit organization dedicated to facilitating & changing conversations around mental health for the safety and belonging of all. The project started in Louisiana and I am excited to bring our programs to San Francisco and beyond. I hope you'll join me for the first in our "Let's Talk About It" series on Sept. 29th. title: Command Line Music - Auwen Workshop
description: This class is an intro to command line music with Auwen, a tool for writing and performing songs in real time using a command line interface. You'll get hands-on experience building tracks from scratch and playing them in a low stakes, collaborative setting. No prior coding or music experience needed. What to expect: installation takes about 5 minutes. Your first beat, maybe an hour. Playing a full set takes a 3-6 weeks of practice depending on experience level. A few students have gone on to perform live sets at SF events and festivals as part of Soniare Collective. With just a bit of dedication you could be next! We would love to have you join our growing family of music producers. After the class you'll be invited to our Discord where we do multiplayer jam sessions, so there's space to keep learning and playing with other people. Workshop Outline Software and sample installation Overview of Auwen User Interface and workflow Multiplayer learning session creating genres you suggest Solo time creating music on your own computer Wrap-up and share resources for further learning Educational Goals To inspire participants and offer an accessible entry point into performing live dance music, while building foundational skills in livecoding, composition, improvisation, and real-time musical decision-making. Instructor Nes Croft is a musician, artist, and computer engineer from Montana who has written and recorded thousands of songs since a young age starting with folk/rock as a teenager and expanding into experimental pop, IDM, techno, and trance. Nes gained an interest in electronics at age 19 after working at the DIY synth company Synthrotek in Portland, OR. Going on to earn a bachelor's degree in computer engineering at Montana State University. While in college Nes co-founded and developed Vaytricks Beat Machine, a mobile drum machine app that received over 100,000 downloads. 5 years later Nes left Vaytricks to pursue a live performance focused approach to music production and Auwen was born. Auwen is a digital audio workstation featuring a hybrid producer/DJ workflow that allows musicians to perform dance music live using a command line interface. Given the nature of the software, Nes naturally gravitated toward live music events testing Auwen at various electronic music festivals in Montana. Later, Nes joined the livecoding scene in San Francisco and started hosting workshops & live music events at TIAT art gallery and Gray Area in San Francisco in 2025-2026. Preparation Bring a laptop/headphones and install the software auwen.app to save time in class. Also bring water and maybe a light snack to keep your energy up because we'll be covering a lot of information! Some drinks may be provided as well. When you arrive come through the front of TIAT then all the way back and down the stairs on the left. The event is in the TIAT basement.

At the heart of this gathering is a simple idea: connection deepens when we feel safe enough to be seen and expressed -not just the polished parts of ourselves, but also the parts we might usually hide or hold back. Through movement, play, somatic awareness, and guided conversations, we'll explore what happens when we let ourselves show up more fully and meet one another more deeply. This is an evolving exploration of connection, community, and play. I'm excited to create a deep experience together and to see what becomes possible when we give ourselves more space to be ourselves and meet one another more fully. title: Robopsychology Salon: What AI Safety Forgets About You
description: SF tech week is about what AI can do. This evening is about what the AI race is doing to us — to our minds, our hearts and our bodies. Psychologist and AI researcher Anna Mikeda works on robopsychology, the psychology of AI minds and of the humans who interact with them. She brings the latest research together, and asks the safety question from the human side: not whether AI turns on us, but what we turn into. Three movements. Minds: cognitive debt — what we stop doing when the model does it for us. Hearts: AI relationships, loneliness, and what an always-available companion does to our tolerance for other people. Bodies: the build loop as a reward loop — instant answers, a model that always agrees, the next project instead of shipping this one, and why it runs on the same architecture that gaming and social media exploit. Then the practical part: what to do about this. Talk, art, open Q&A, and tools you can use. For builders, users, and anyone who has noticed their own attention changing.

computational poetry reading group: game poems
description: Our guest curator this month is Rachel Heleva, a game designer and researcher, and Executive Director of the MADE. What happens when a poem becomes something you can play? When rules, choices, repetition, chance, constraint, and computation become part of how a poem makes meaning? And from the other direction, when does a game begin to behave like a poem? Game Poems brings together writers, artists, and game makers working between poetry and play for an evening of short readings, performances, demonstrations, and works in progress. We’ll encounter games made from language, poems structured by rules, computational literature, interactive fiction, and other forms that trouble the boundary between reading and playing. Rachel will also share a prototype of In Countless Shadows, which treats Shakespeare’s sonnets as playable systems. The presentations will be followed by a conversation facilitated by Helen Shewolfe Tseng. For more on the strange territory between videogames and poetry, explore https://www.gamepoems.com/. computational poetry reading group is a recurring series of gatherings at the intersection of language and technology.
